message.reasoning:
I need to choose between paying the $50 jail fine or rolling for doubles.

I have $1157 and no monopolies. Player 3 holds all four railroads and a pink monopoly, while player 1 has an orange monopoly but almost no cash. I am considering the risk of rolling doubles versus paying the fine.

I already failed one doubles roll. If I fail again, I must pay the $50 fine. I will keep rolling for now.

Rolling from jail would land on St. Charles, States Avenue, or Virginia. Paying the fine now would leave $1107 before the roll.

Rolling from jail would hit the pink monopoly at $200–$220 with two houses, or the orange monopoly at $90–$100 with one house. I am weighing these rent costs against paying the $50 fine now.

I am double-checking the exact orange monopoly rent schedule. Player 3 paid $200 rent to player 1 on Tennessee before player 1 built additional houses on St. James and Tennessee.

The $200 rent on Tennessee does not match standard one-house or two-house orange monopoly rates. Player 1 currently has two houses on St. James, three on Tennessee, and two on New York. I am now using the current holdings to determine the exact rent schedule.

The $200 rent on Tennessee does not match classic one-house or two-house orange monopoly rates. Player 4 paid $180 on Virginia at turn 87, which also conflicts with the current two-house holdings. These discrepancies suggest the game may use a simplified or non-standard rent table.

Player 4 paid $180 on Virginia with two houses, which is below the classic $220 rate. Player 1 paid $200 on Pennsylvania Railroad, matching standard four-railroad rent. Player 3 paid $200 on Tennessee at turn 81, but that transaction occurred before player 1 built additional houses on St. James and Tennessee.

I will use the observed rent amounts as my danger estimates, treating classic rates only as upper bounds.

I estimate the pink monopoly at roughly $160–$180 per house, and St. Charles at a lower rate. A three-house Tennessee could cost about $550. I will stay in jail until forced, since I have no monopolies to earn rent from.

Opponents are bleeding cash while I sit safe. Player 1 has $15 and player 4 has $94. I have one more free doubles roll before the third turn forces payment. I will stay in jail.

Dark blue properties are unreachable from jail. The expected cost of leaving is roughly $180–$200, with the highest risk on the pink monopoly.

Rolling an 8 from jail would hit Tennessee with three houses, costing roughly $500–$700. A roll of 9 would land on New York with two houses for about $250–$300. Rolling a 10 lands on Free Parking for nothing. Buying Kentucky is not worthwhile because I lack the other yellows to complete the set, and giving p3 another trade piece is undesirable.

Leaving jail would cost roughly $150–$250 in rent plus the $50 fine. A roll of 8 on Tennessee with three houses could bankrupt me at about $700, leaving only $400. Paying that to player 1 would give them enough cash to rebuild their orange monopoly and become dangerous again. Player 4 is nearly broke. Staying in jail prevents player 1 from using that rent to recover.
